case_name: Ningappa Yallappa Hosamani and Others v State of Karnataka and Others

statutes.act: Read With Section 149 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: The occurrence took place in the intervening night of 31.1.2005 around midnight.
Namadev Muralidhar Huvvannavar (the deceased) resided in Bommanabudni village along with his wife-Girijabai (PW.1) and his five children, out of whom Panduranga (PW.5) is one.

He was an accused in a session case on the allegation of having committed about ten years prior to 2005, the murder of Arjunappa Yaraddi (father of accused No.4) having set on fire the sugarcane crop of Yallappa Yaraddi.
On 30.1.2005 he left for Mudhol at about 4.00 p.m., on his CD Don motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 48/E-1688 (M.0.15).
He did not return home on that day and on the next day as well.
Therefore, Girijabai (P.W.1) and Panduranga. (P-W.5) started the search for help.
petitioner_arguments: The circumstances relied on clearly established the accusations and the only case is recovery under Section 27 of Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
On the basis of statement made under Section 27 of the Evidence Act the conviction cannot be maintained because it cannot be said that the circumstances have been established.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution relied on the recovery of the motorcycle in furtherance of the voluntary information furnished by the accused No.6.

It was submitted by the State that perhaps it may be a typographical mistake and it may be the accused Nos.1 and 2 since the records show that it is the accused Nos.1 and 2, who had been arrested on 3.2.2005.
court_reasoning: The cumulative effect of the circumstantial evidence concluded that the prosecution had proved that it was the accused who had committed the murder of Namadev and had disposed of the dead body by putting it in a gunny bag and burying it near the canal of Chickakhandi village and throwing motor cycle in the river.
We find no reason to discard the alleged recovery of motorcycle in furtherance of the information furnished by accused No.6.
holding: The conviction of A-3 to A-5 was set aside as noted above.
A-6 and A-7 were acquitted of all charges relating to Section 302 and 109 read with Section 149 IPC.
The conviction of A-1 and A-3 under Sections 302 and 109 read with Section 149 IPC was converted to Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC.
cases_cited: Ningappa Yallappa Hosamani and Others v State of Karnataka
